import re

with open('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_13/projects/contamcal-irt-calibration/artifacts/paper_draft/references.bib') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Parse entries
entries = re.split(r'(?=@)', content)
results = []
for entry in entries:
    year_match = re.search(r'year\s*=\s*\{(\d+)\}', entry)
    if not year_match:
        continue
    year = int(year_match.group(1))
    if year < 2025:
        continue
    
    key_match = re.search(r'@\w+\{([^,]+)', entry)
    title_match = re.search(r'title\s*=\s*\{(.+?)\}', entry)
    author_match = re.search(r'author\s*=\s*\{(.+?)\}', entry)
    url_match = re.search(r'url\s*=\s*\{(.+?)\}', entry)
    
    key = key_match.group(1).strip() if key_match else 'UNKNOWN'
    title = title_match.group(1).strip() if title_match else 'NO_TITLE'
    author = author_match.group(1).strip()[:80] if author_match else 'NO_AUTHOR'
    url = url_match.group(1).strip() if url_match else 'NO_URL'
    
    results.append((key, year, author, title[:100], url))

# Already verified keys
verified = {'dong2026dose', 'yang2026rl', 'gu2026psnirt', 'polo2026growing', 'rao2026silicon', 'han2026probing', 'jerzak2026', 'choi_2025_kds', 'li_2025_dcr', 'xu2025emperor'}

print(f'Total 2025+ entries: {len(results)}')
print(f'Already verified: {len([r for r in results if r[0] in verified])}')
print(f'Need verification: {len([r for r in results if r[0] not in verified])}')
print()
print('=== NEED VERIFICATION ===')
for i, (key, year, author, title, url) in enumerate(results):
    if key not in verified:
        print(f'{i+1}. [{key}] ({year}) {author[:40]}')
        print(f'   Title: {title}')
        print(f'   URL: {url}')
        print()
"

content.text: 10:Item Response Theory (IRT) has gained traction as a principled alternative to raw accuracy for comparing LLMs. \citet{lalor_2024_irt_nlp} provide a comprehensive tutorial on IRT in NLP evaluation, covering model selection, parameter estimation, and ability scoring. TinyBenchmarks \citep{polo_2024_tinybenchmarks} exploits IRT-informed item selection to reduce evaluation cost while preserving ranking fidelity across diverse model families. Growing Pains \citep{habba_2025_growing_pains} validates IRT at scale on 400+ models with fixed parameter calibration and identifies practical limitations in low-respondent regimes where item parameters become poorly constrained. HiBayES \citep{luettgau_2025_hibayes} extends IRT with hierarchical Bayesian inference to produce credible intervals over ability estimates, enabling principled model comparison under uncertainty. ATLAS \citep{li_2024_atlas} applies IRT for adaptive testing and selects maximally informative items to reduce per-model evaluation cost. Across this body of work, all items are treated as equally trustworthy: none models contamination as a covariate within the item response function. ContamCal augments IRT with per-domain contamination parameters $\gamma_d$ that separate genuine ability from exposure-driven inflation.
